decisions.reason: Fouling detection automation builds on the firm's control and energy-recovery know-how, and its own R&D and university links let it interpret early field data and refine the offer instead of abandoning it.
The weir-dimensioning web tool codifies the firm's documented hydraulic project experience on existing IT modules, is cheap to maintain, and supports sales of the new flap weirs and gates.
The fouling detection system overlaps with Product A, so it may eventually be merged into it, but it fits the energy-recovery strategy that the firm's research cooperation helps it develop.
A spring-controlled flap weir lies very close to the firm's core hydraulic steel-engineering competence, so the firm can readily assimilate customer feedback and improve the design.
An energy management system for water facilities directly serves the firm's digital-networking and efficiency strategy and draws on its existing automation software base.
The overflow flap gate line with several models has its own page and sits in the firm's established water-level regulation business, which signals strong commitment and low risk.
